questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_PT_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

A survey asks students to report their favorite school lunch. What type of data is collected?

feedback.text: No numerical measurement or count is recorded for each student.
Only one variable is recorded, and it is categorical.
Relative frequency is a summary proportion, not the original data type.
Favorite lunch is a category label, not a measured amount.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_PT_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

A data set records hours studied and quiz score for each student. Which display is most appropriate for exploring the relationship?

feedback.text: A scatterplot shows the relationship between two numerical variables.
A pie chart shows parts of a whole for one categorical variable.
A one-way frequency table would not show the relationship between two numerical variables.

answer.text: Box plot of one variable only

feedback.text: A single box plot would summarize one numerical variable, not the relationship.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_PT_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.2

A histogram interval from 20 to 29 minutes has a bar height of 7. What does the height represent?

feedback.text: The bar height is a frequency, not the mean.

answer.text: Seven values fall in the 20 to 29 minute interval

feedback.text: Histogram bar height shows the frequency for that interval.
The interval width comes from the endpoints, not the bar height.
A histogram shows numerical intervals, not category labels.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_PT_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.DVD.3

A relative frequency table shows that 35% of Grade 9 students ride the bus. In a segmented bar graph, how much of the Grade 9 bar should the bus segment occupy?

feedback.text: 65% is the complement, not the listed bus relative frequency.
This moves the decimal incorrectly.
The whole bar is 100%, but bus is only one segment.
Segment length should match the relative frequency for that category.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_PT_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display is usually appropriate for one numerical variable such as daily step counts?

feedback.text: A dot plot can show the distribution of one numerical variable.
A two-way table organizes two categorical variables.
A pie chart shows categorical parts of a whole.
A segmented bar graph compares categorical proportions across groups.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_PT_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.2

A bar chart shows favorite study method. The tallest bar is online videos. What conclusion is supported?

answer.text: Online videos caused students to earn higher grades

feedback.text: The display shows preference counts, not cause and effect.
Other bars may still have responses.

answer.text: Online videos had the greatest number of responses among the listed methods

feedback.text: The tallest category bar represents the greatest frequency.

answer.text: Online videos is a numerical variable

feedback.text: Favorite study method is categorical.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_PT_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.DVD.3

Why are relative frequencies useful when comparing groups with different totals?

answer.text: They remove the need for category labels

feedback.text: Category labels are still needed to interpret the display.

answer.text: They compare proportions fairly across groups

feedback.text: Relative frequencies account for different group sizes.

answer.text: They prove that one category caused another

feedback.text: Relative frequencies describe data; they do not prove causation.

answer.text: They make every raw count equal

feedback.text: Relative frequencies do not change the original counts.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_PT_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which data situation is bivariate categorical?

feedback.text: This is one numerical variable.

answer.text: Grade level and preferred lunch option

feedback.text: Both variables are categorical.
These are two numerical variables.

answer.text: Number of pets owned by each student

feedback.text: This is one numerical variable.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_PT_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.2

Before interpreting a graph, which components should be checked first?

answer.text: Only the color of the bars

feedback.text: Color alone does not define the meaning of the data.
The largest value needs labels, units, and context to be meaningful.

answer.text: Title, labels, units, scale, and context

feedback.text: These components explain what the display and quantities mean.

answer.text: Only whether the graph looks neat

feedback.text: Visual neatness does not guarantee correct interpretation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_PT_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.DVD.3

A segmented bar graph shows Grade 10 has a larger car segment than Grade 9. What is a supported interpretation?

answer.text: Grade 10 has a greater proportion of students choosing car

feedback.text: A larger segment means a larger relative frequency for that category.

answer.text: Grade 10 must have more total students

feedback.text: Segmented percent bars compare proportions, not necessarily total counts.

answer.text: Car choice caused students to be in Grade 10

feedback.text: The graph does not show cause and effect.
A smaller segment may still represent some Grade 9 students.
